source.name: usp_GetTopCustomers
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE   PROCEDURE dbo.usp_GetTopCustomers
    @TopN INT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    SELECT TOP (@TopN)
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        ISNULL(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        DATEDIFF(DAY, MAX(o.OrderDate), GETDATE()) AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.usp_GetTopCustomers(
    p_TopN INT
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    CustomerID INT,
    FullName TEXT,
    OrderCount BIGINT,
    TotalSpent NUMERIC,
    DaysSinceLastOrder INT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        COALESCE(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - MAX(o.OrderDate)))::INT AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC
    LIMIT p_TopN;
END;
$$;
assumptions: The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL or will be created
CustomerID column is of type INT in both Customers and Orders tables
FirstName and LastName are text-compatible types (VARCHAR, TEXT, etc.)
TotalAmount is a numeric type (DECIMAL, NUMERIC, or similar)
OrderDate is a DATE or TIMESTAMP type
The procedure returns a result set, so it's converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't send row count messages by default)
Parameter renamed from @TopN to p_TopN following PostgreSQL naming conventions

reviewFlags.reason: Verify the actual data type of CustomerID in the Customers and Orders tables. It might be BIGINT, SERIAL, or another integer type.
Verify the actual data type and precision of TotalAmount in the Orders table. May need to specify NUMERIC(precision, scale) for exact compatibility.

The DATEDIFF conversion assumes OrderDate is a DATE or TIMESTAMP. If it's a different type, casting may be required. Also, this calculation may return NULL for customers with no orders, unlike SQL Server which would handle it differently.
Confirm that the dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL typically uses 'public' as the default schema. Consider whether schema qualification is needed.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server uses '+' for string concatenation while PostgreSQL uses '||'. The conversion has been applied.
ISNULL() converted to COALESCE(). Both functions behave similarly but COALESCE is SQL standard and can accept multiple arguments.

DATEDIFF(DAY, ..., GETDATE()) converted to EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - ...)). The behavior is similar but PostgreSQL interval arithmetic may handle edge cases differently, especially with NULL values.
SQL Server's TOP converted to PostgreSQL's LIMIT. Both limit result sets but LIMIT is applied after ORDER BY, which matches the SQL Server behavior in this case.
SQL Server procedure returns result set implicitly. PostgreSQL requires explicit FUNCTION with RETURNS TABLE and RETURN QUERY statement.
For customers with no orders, DaysSinceLastOrder will be NULL in PostgreSQL (due to MAX returning NULL). SQL Server DATEDIFF with NULL also returns NULL, so behavior should be consistent.
